label: Solo fallback
description: What a lone player can do in a multi-seat unit.

terms.label: Full control
terms.description: Alone, the player drives and still fires a weapon: the driver seat's own weapons, or a weapon the source hands to a lone driver. Weapons in other seats either pass to the driver or wait for a teammate; say which in crew notes.
examples: C&C Renegade: the driver takes over the weapon whenever the gunner seat is empty
Battlefield tanks and attack helicopters: the driver keeps the main gun or the rockets, while the second seat's gun waits for a teammate
PlanetSide 2: a lone Liberator pilot fires the nose gun and may hop to the belly gun mid-fight; the tail gun waits for a teammate

terms.label: Seat swap
terms.description: Alone, the player must change seats to shoot, because no weapon works from the driver seat: drive or shoot, not both.
examples: PlanetSide 2: the Sunderer's driver has no gun, so a lone driver hops into a gun seat to fight

terms.label: Auto-gunner
terms.description: Empty gun seats fire on their own at reduced accuracy until a player takes them.
examples: Halo campaign: computer-controlled gunners man the turret

terms.label: Needs crew
terms.description: Even by changing seats, a lone player can't do a core job, such as firing the main gun, because the source needs two seats working at once.

tie_breaks.rule: Ask what one player alone can do, in this order. (1) The source makes empty gun seats fire by themselves: auto-gunner. (2) A lone driver can still fire something, their own weapon or one the source hands over: full-control, even when other seats' guns go quiet. (3) A lone player can reach the guns by changing seats, even slowly: seat-swap. (4) Otherwise: needs-crew. A proposal crew is always full-control (decision 2A).
